text.p: Preliminary U.S. damage assessments indicate that the cruise missile attack on military targets in southern Iraq was "effective", a senior Pentagon military official said on Tuesday.
"We certainly have indications that, by all means, the raid was effective," U.S. Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston, deputy chairman of the military Joint Chiefs of Staff, told reporters.

Ralston said at a Pentagon news conference that the military did not have "a complete assessment of the battle damage done as yet." But responding to statements by Iraq's President Saddam Hussein that many of the missiles were shot down, the general said that there was no indication that any of the 27 missiles was downed or had malfunctioned.
"We have no evidence that there was any misfiring of the missiles," he told reporters of the strikes against Iraqi radars, anti-aircraft missiles and air defence targets in southern Iraq.
